# Project memory

Durable decisions for this repo, written for any coding agent (Claude Code,
Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini). Read this before changing content, generated
data, or the portfolio chat.

`CLAUDE.md` documents **how** the code works. This file records **what was
decided and why**, including things the code cannot show you — what was
deliberately left out, and what must not be regenerated by hand.

Add an entry when a decision would surprise the next agent. Date every entry.
Delete an entry when it stops being true; do not leave a stale one behind.

## Generated files — never hand-edit

- `src/data/resume.json` — written by `pnpm update:resume` from the Google Doc,
  which is the single source of truth. Overwritten on every run.
- `src/data/wiki.generated.json` — written by `pnpm wiki` (and `prebuild`) from
  `content/wiki/*.md`. The Markdown is the source of truth.
- `src/data/projects.generated.json` — written by the same script, from the same
  Markdown. It is what `/projects` renders.

Editing either by hand looks like it works and is silently reverted by the next
build.

## Decisions

### 2026-08-13 — the resume comes from a new Google Doc, laid out differently

The source doc moved to `1oxn2bRkMuQwXhhtCsQjGh1nOx8IgZ9ME9H8p7iNnJrM`. It is a
rewrite, not a copy, and three things about its shape broke the parser rather
than merely changing the content:

- **Company and dates share one line** (`Overtone.art, Charlotte, NC | 03/2026 –
Present`) where the old doc put the dates on their own line between the role
  and the company. The job anchor is that combined line now.
- **It contains no hyperlinks at all.** The contact details and the employer
  sites used to be `<a>` tags; they are plain text, or absent. Hence the bare
  domains being given a scheme in `parseHeader`, and `COMPANY_URL` in the
  parser holding the four employer links the cards used to get from the doc.
  Those four came from the old doc's own hyperlinks — they are not guesses.
  **Do not derive an employer URL from a company name.** Centralex and LIX are
  named as `.com` domains and would resolve to whoever owns those today.
- **Education is one line**, `<field> — <school>`, and no longer carries years.
  `education[].years` is now empty, and the static resume prints no dates there.

The doc still has no `Summary:` or `Tech:` lines, so every card's one-liner and
every chip is derived — the run says so, and that is the state it has always
been in, not a regression from the move.

`siteConfig.tagline` ("Senior Frontend & Full-Stack Engineer") is hand-written
and no longer matches the doc's title ("Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer").
It was left alone deliberately — it is the SEO description, not resume content —
but the two should not drift much further apart.

### 2026-08-13 — the scene shows what fits in a circle; the resume shows everything

The new doc's TECHNICAL SKILLS section is much longer than the old one (56
entries, up from 30) and prose-ier: "schema design", "code review", "npm package
publishing", "end-to-end testing". Every entry becomes a disc in the stack ball
and is eligible to become a card chip, and a disc has room for a logo or about
four characters — `StackBallDisc.abbreviate` was rendering "migrations" as
"migr" and "Docker" as "Dock", which name nothing.

So `model.ts` keeps a disc or chip only if the label **has a logo, or is short
enough to read whole** (4 characters for a disc, 5 for a chip). Sixteen prose
entries drop out of the scene; one text disc is left, "SQL".

**This hides a disc, not a skill, and the distinction is the point.** `SKILLS`
and `CHIPS` stay whole — the static resume prints all 56 in full, and `/llms.txt`
and the JSON-LD read `resume.json` directly, so nothing a recruiter or an agent
reads disagrees with the PDF. Do not "tidy up" by filtering at the parser; that
is where the site would start lying about the doc.

Two renames do belong in the parser, in `SKILL_DISPLAY`, because they are the
same technology under a longer name rather than a different one: `React 19` →
`React` (the doc lists both, so it deduplicates) and
`Model Context Protocol (MCP)` → `MCP`.

The other lever is `tech-logos.json`. A label with a logo is kept whatever its
length, so mapping one is how a long name earns its disc back. Eighteen entries
were added for the new doc's spellings — `Node.js`, `Tailwind CSS`, `Docker`,
`Redis`, `MySQL`, `Prisma`, `TypeORM`, `Express`, `Vitest`, `Prettier`,
`Turborepo`, `shadcn/ui`, `TanStack Query` and four aliases of names already
mapped. Several only lacked a logo because the new doc spells them differently
than the old one did (`Node` → `Node.js`, `Tailwind` → `Tailwind CSS`), which is
the failure mode to check first when a familiar technology loses its disc.
`Zustand`, `WebSockets` and `REST APIs` have no Simple Icons entry and stay out.

### 2026-08-13 — the projects wiki lives in this repo and is published

`~/projects/projects-wiki` was moved in as `content/wiki/`, rather than kept as a
subtree, submodule, or CI checkout. The site deploys with the corpus and needs no
extra credentials.

Consequence: the corpus is served verbatim at `/llms-full.txt` and summarised in
`/llms.txt`. **Adding a page to `content/wiki/projects/` is a decision to publish
it.** Review a change there as a public change. Keep runbooks, environment files,
audit reports, customer data, analytics, and commercial planning out of it.

### 2026-08-13 — the corpus is 23 pages, deliberately

Five project pages were held back from publication when the wiki was moved in:
`mood`, `willy`, `bake-app`, `gtm`, `pitchsite` (31 → 26). Three more were
withdrawn once the page was generated from the corpus and the owner saw the full
list rendered: `aso-audit-agent`, `accordsq`, `vocallq` (26 → 23) — all three
archived experiments, and the weakest evidence on a page read by recruiters.
The Markdown is backed up at `~/projects/homepage/wiki-backup-2026-08-13/`,
outside the repo and not committed. `index.md` and `technologies.md` were
rewritten to fold Mood into Overtone, so nothing dangles.

Each of the five was held back for its own reason, and the reasons are the rule
for anything added later. The audience is recruiters and hiring managers (see the
design context in `CLAUDE.md`), so the test is not "is this good engineering" —
all five were — but "how does this read to the person deciding whether to
interview me".

- **willy** — a live interview coach that listens and privately suggests answers,
  with a desktop overlay. Published on a site built for recruiters, it reads as
  interview-cheating infrastructure.
- **gtm** — scrapes public GitHub code for prospect signals. Reads as lead
  harvesting; the page's own defensive wording ("no automated send", "stores no
  harvested personal contact data") is the tell.
- **pitchsite** — finds local businesses with weak websites and generates
  unsolicited pitch sites. Cold-outreach adjacency, and only a proof of concept.
- **bake-app** — a real operating business's platform. Confidentiality, not
  taste: publishing a client's system needs their consent, not a judgment call.
- **mood** — no risk at all. It is a surface inside the Overtone monorepo, and
  four pages describing one platform diluted it. Folded into `overtone.md`
  (aliases, overview sentence, a "Mood surface" technology bullet), so a question
  about Mood still retrieves.

Do not "restore" a missing page from that backup or from history without asking —
their absence is the decision. Bringing one back means three things together: the
`.md` file, its references in `index.md` and `technologies.md`, then `pnpm wiki`.

Withdrawing one is the same list plus a fourth. The `.md`, its line in
`index.md`, its mentions in `technologies.md` — **including any technology it was
the last carrier of** (Mastra, ONNX and Shopify Skia went with those three, and
React Native is now Overtone's alone) — and any _other page's card_ that names
it. `stream-schema`'s card cited the ASO audit and had to be rewritten: a card
pointing at a page the chat cannot load advertises the gap instead of closing it.

### 2026-08-13 — a dictation plugin split out of Willy is published standalone

If the dictation part of Willy becomes its own repo, it gets a page — on-device
speech-to-text is neutral, strong evidence (local Whisper/sherpa-onnx runtimes,
ONNX Runtime, audio loopback capture, Kotlin native modules, secure IPC, platform
adapters). What was withheld was the use case, not the technology.

Its page must not name Willy or describe itself as extracted from anything. The
WallSnap page can say "extracted from a gallery feature" because Overtone is
published; a pointer to `willy` resolves to nothing, and the chat is instructed to
answer "that page was not loaded", which advertises the gap instead of closing it.
Write fresh prose — the backup's copy carries "live interview coach", "suggestion
routing", "live overlays", "preventing fabrication or impersonation". Two more
things when it lands: it must genuinely be a separate repo, or `source_scope:`
either lies or names Willy; and re-add **Whisper and ONNX** to
`technologies.md` — Willy was Whisper's only carrier, and vocallQ was ONNX's, so
neither is listed any more.

### 2026-08-13 — `private: true` alongside a `public_url` is not a contradiction

`mcpmake` carries both, and correctly: `mcpmake@0.4.10` is public on npm and
`mcpmake.dev` is live, while `github.com/starkyru/mcpmake-cli` is private (404
from the API). The badge describes the source, not the product. Verified rather
than assumed — do not "fix" it.

`beta: true` alongside `public_url` is the same shape and is the one on
`wallsnap`, `angleforge` and `timerail`: go there, it works, it is not finished.
It must agree with `status:` — those three read "preparing store submission",
"invite-only" and "release candidate under validation". A card and a status must
not tell a visitor and the chat different stories.

### 2026-08-13 — /projects is generated from the wiki, not hand-kept

The projects page had its own hand-written list in
`src/components/projects/sections.ts`. It had drifted nine projects behind the
corpus: the chat could describe WallSnap, Countersign, Timerail, Gallery SaaS,
Agent Signals, Spendgate, Frontend Debugger, Skills and the homepage itself,
while the page a visitor reads did not mention them. The list is now compiled
from `content/wiki/` alongside the corpus, and `sections.ts` only re-exports it.

Consequence: **adding a page to `content/wiki/projects/` now also lists it on
`/projects`.** Publishing and listing are one decision. Front matter carries the
card (`card:`, `tools:`, `repo:`, `private:`, `public_url:`); grouping and order
come from `index.md`.

Card copy is written in the page's voice — first person, concrete, plain — not
the wiki's formal register, because it is read by a person scanning a page
rather than by a model assembling an answer. The 17 blurbs that predate this
change were carried over rather than regenerated; that voice is the reference
for any new one.

Two artifacts on purpose: the browser gets `projects.generated.json` and never
the ~100 KB of page bodies in `wiki.generated.json`.

### 2026-08-13 — chat retrieval is deterministic, not embeddings

Page selection is exact name, alias, and technology matching over the corpus
(`src/lib/wiki/retrieval.ts`). It is auditable, costs nothing per request, and
cannot drift. Do not introduce a vector store, embedding index, or extra service
for this until the corpus is substantially larger than a few dozen pages.

### 2026-08-13 — the visitor's question selects trusted pages, never joins them

Visitor text is scored against the wiki and used only to choose which pages are
sent. It never becomes part of the reference material, and the retrieved pages
travel as a separate trusted message. Any change to the chat must preserve that
boundary. The pages behind an answer come back as `sources` and are shown under
it, so a claim can be checked.
